reviewer.role: independent OSS governance and commercial-boundary reviewer

acceptance: All promised OSS capabilities usable offline; commercial hypotheses not represented as proven sales.

requirements.requirement: The complete promised local framework, component, security/accessibility, protocol, Studio/DevTools and testkit capabilities remain Apache-2.0 rather than paid entitlements.
evidence: MASTER-SOT.md section 21, docs/15-oss-business.md, docs/business/oss-commercial-boundary.md and docs/public/0.1.0-support-boundary.md agree on the boundary.
The exact six public RC archives declare Apache-2.0 and contain byte-identical canonical LICENSE and NOTICE files.
The internal testkit remains a private Apache-2.0 source workspace, preventing release-only helpers from being represented as a seventh public API.
T27 and the final T32 system review are complete and their retained manifests are hash-bound below.

requirements.requirement: Ordinary local use has no account, license-server callback, paid row cap, mandatory model call, or hidden audit transport.
evidence: An independent external consumer installed the exact six tarball integrities and strict-checked all 130 export specifiers.

Core parsing, bounded local audit export, web server, protocol, DevTools and React SSR entry points executed with fetch, HTTP, HTTPS, net and DNS blocked; zero network attempt occurred before explicit positive-control probes.
Fresh audit tests passed 6/6 and fresh site browser tests passed 6/6, including local no-model flows and default-no-egress governance pages.
Static inspection found network effects only in the documented optional runtime HTTP, model/provider and MCP paths; the web registry explicitly does not fetch or discover sources.

requirements.requirement: Commercial operation and support are hypotheses, not evidence of sales, availability or market validation.
evidence: README, business/public boundary documents, SUPPORT, SECURITY and site legal copy state that hosted service, pricing, SLA, demand, recurring revenue and product-market fit are not claimed for 0.1.0.
Future hosted collaboration, governance, retained audit search, managed infrastructure and support are consistently described as possible separate services using the public contracts.
No customer, contract, price, revenue, demand, certification, partner, availability or SLA assertion was found in the reviewed release-facing materials.

requirements.requirement: Governance and availability statements match observed project state.
evidence: CONTRIBUTING requires Apache-2.0 inbound contributions and DCO 1.1 sign-off without claiming a CLA; TRADEMARKS preserves the Apache-2.0 mark boundary without claiming certification.
GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled, public Issues are disabled, and SECURITY/SUPPORT promise neither a monitored email/queue nor a response-time SLA.

All six RC registry identities returned 404 and the production site reports the older 6b0c4f0 revision; release-facing copy explicitly separates source, registry and production state, so neither is represented as current-candidate availability.

priorRiskRecheck.auditExporter: closed: fixed event families and codes, strict runtime validation, bounded oldest eviction with count/byte disclosure, fail-closed redacted clock behavior, clear/dispose release, and no audit-owned network/filesystem I/O
priorRiskRecheck.licenseAndNotices: closed: canonical Apache-2.0 LICENSE and NOTICE are present in each exact public archive and in the private testkit source
priorRiskRecheck.commercialTruthfulness: closed: future commercial surfaces are explicitly conditional and are not represented as current service, sale, demand, price, SLA, revenue or product-market fit
priorRiskRecheck.availabilityTruthfulness: closed for T35: local source/candidate, registry and deployed-site states are distinguished; publication and deployment remain separate release tasks

limitations: This is a source- and RC-bound sampled audit, not universal certification that every optional integration or environment is offline-capable.
Optional authenticated HTTP, MCP and BYOK/provider paths intentionally use host-authorized network effects and are not contradicted by the offline local-path acceptance.

SECURITY's phrase that source, registry packages and the deployed site have separate release evidence must be read with README, SUPPORT and the boundary documents: it distinguishes evidence domains and does not claim that this RC is published or deployed.

The registry and production observations are time-bound. They do not reserve 0.1.0-rc.1, approve publication, qualify provenance, promote a dist-tag, deploy the reviewed source, or establish commercial availability.

Manual assistive-technology certification, general model answer quality, registry publication, source release, staging/production deployment and stable promotion remain outside T35 and are not claimed.

verdict.summary: No P0, P1 or P2 governance, commercial-boundary or offline-local-use finding remains in the inspected T35 scope. The exact RC bytes and current source satisfy T35 acceptance with the stated limits.
